collection: Primary4 Igbo self-description, personal letters and greetings
note: Twelve original structured drafts: ten written tasks and two live/recorded spoken interactions, eight limited author mappings. Original letter stimuli and fictional identities. No tone-discrimination model, real addresses, meetings, native academic approval or actual classroom performance claimed.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Identify verbs that express identity and residence in simple self-description sentences.
questions.prompt: Gụọ ahịrịokwu ndị a. Depụta ngwaa dị n’ahịrịokwu nke ọ bụla. Kọwaa ihe ngwaa nke ọ bụla na-egosi ebe a.
questions.answer: bụ; bi. “bụ” na-egosi aha onye ahụ. “bi” na-egosi ebe onye ahụ bi.
questions.explanation: Identity and residence are expressed by different verbs; a verb need not describe a visible physical action.

markingGuide.description: Identifies bụ in the first sentence.
Identifies bi in the second sentence.
Explains the identity function of bụ in this context in intelligible Igbo.
Explains that bi expresses living/residence in intelligible Igbo.

questions.languageReviewNote: Independent Igbo linguistic/academic review is pending. Underdots are meaningful; these contextual writing tasks do not prescribe a complete tone-marking system. Accept equivalent intelligible Igbo forms and regional variants after examiner checking. Local school orthographic conventions and marking calibration remain unverified.
questions.passage: Aha m bụ Nkem. M bi na Nsukka.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Write coherent simple sentences describing oneself in a stated situation.
questions.prompt: Ị batara n’otu ọhụrụ n’ụlọ akwụkwọ. Dee ahịrịokwu atọ n’asụsụ Igbo iji kọwaa onwe gị: aha gị, ebe i bi na ihe ị na-agụ. Ị nwere ike iji aha na ebe i chepụtara.
questions.answer: Aha m bụ Kamsi. M bi na Aba. Ana m agụ akwụkwọ gbasara osisi.
questions.explanation: The three sentences introduce one speaker and supply three different requested details. This is an illustrative fictional response, not a required identity.

markingGuide.description: Gives a name in a complete intelligible Igbo sentence.
States a place of residence using a fictional place if preferred.
States something being read, with an appropriate verb form.
Maintains one speaker and uses meaningful sentence boundaries.

questions.languageReviewNote: Independent Igbo linguistic/academic review is pending. Underdots are meaningful; these contextual writing tasks do not prescribe a complete tone-marking system. Accept equivalent intelligible Igbo forms and regional variants after examiner checking. Local school orthographic conventions and marking calibration remain unverified.
questions.teacherSupport: Use a fictional name and town; no home address or other personal disclosure is required. “Ihe ị na-agụ” asks what you are reading; accept an appropriate book/topic or course of study.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Write coherent simple sentences describing oneself in a stated situation.
questions.prompt: Chika na-ede maka onwe ya. Degharịa ederede a ka onye na-ekwu okwu ghara ịgbanwe. Debe aha, ebe obibi na ihe ọ na-eme.
questions.answer: Aha m bụ Chika. M bi na Aba. M na-agụ akwụkwọ.
questions.explanation: The middle sentence changes to a third-person subject. Revising it into first person restores a consistent self-description while retaining the other information.

markingGuide.description: Changes the residence sentence to first person, such as M bi na Aba.
Preserves the name, town and reading activity without introducing another speaker.
Writes a coherent Igbo version with clear sentence boundaries.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Describe oneself and answer relevant questions in a short Igbo conversation.
questions.prompt: Gị na onye nkụzi ga-akparịta ụka n’asụsụ Igbo. Kọwaa onwe gị nkenke. Zaa ajụjụ abụọ onye nkụzi ga-ajụ gị. Jiri aha na ebe i chepụtara ma ọ bụrụ na ịchọrọ.
questions.answer: Aha m bụ Zikora. M bi na Enugu. Ana m agụ akwụkwọ. Onye nkụzi: Kedụ aha gị? Zikora: Aha m bụ Zikora. Onye nkụzi: Kedụ ebe i bi? Zikora: M bi na Enugu.
questions.explanation: The learner must actually produce a short introduction and respond to a partner. The sample is one possible interaction; repeating a prepared text without responding does not meet all criteria.

markingGuide.description: Gives an intelligible short Igbo introduction with at least two relevant details.
Responds appropriately to the examiner’s name question.
Responds appropriately to the examiner’s residence question.
Maintains intelligible turn-taking; allow self-correction and equivalent forms.

questions.teacherSupport: Examiner asks “Kedụ aha gị?” and “Kedụ ebe i bi?” after the introduction. Use a fictional identity and town. Permit an equivalent question form; do not require personal addresses.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Explain personal-letter communication using a suitable familiar recipient and purpose.
questions.prompt: Gịnị bụ leta nkeonye? Nye otu ihe mere ị ga-eji degara enyi gị ụdị leta a.
questions.answer: Leta nkeonye bụ leta mmadụ na-edegara onye ọ maara, dịka enyi ya. Enwere m ike ide ya iji kelee enyi m maka enyemaka ya.
questions.explanation: A familiar recipient and a personal communicative purpose distinguish this use of a letter from a general public announcement. The examples do not exhaust possible recipients or purposes.

markingGuide.description: Explains in intelligible Igbo that the letter is addressed personally to a familiar person, such as a friend or relative.
Gives a suitable personal purpose, such as thanks, sharing news, a request or invitation.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Identify and organise the greeting, body and closing of a personal letter.
questions.prompt: N’ime leta a, họpụta ekele, otu ahịrịokwu dị n’etiti leta na mmechi. Kọwaa otu ọrụ mmechi na-arụ.
questions.answer: Ekele: Ezigbo enyi m Oziọma. Otu ahịrịokwu n’etiti: Daalụ maka akwụkwọ ị nyere m. Mmechi: Enyi gị, Ikenna. Mmechi na-egosi na leta agwụla ma na-akọ onye dere ya.
questions.explanation: The greeting addresses the recipient, the body carries the message and the ending closes and identifies the sender. Accept another body sentence from this original letter.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the salutation addressing Oziọma.
Selects a complete body sentence from the supplied letter.
Identifies the closing and sender, Enyi gị / Ikenna.
Explains an appropriate closing function in Igbo.

Ụlọ Akwụkwọ Mmụta,
Aba.

Ezigbo enyi m Oziọma,

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Identify and organise the greeting, body and closing of a personal letter.
questions.prompt: A gwakọtara akụkụ leta Ugo. Dee mkpụrụedemede A, B na C n’usoro kwesịrị ekwesị, malite n’ekele ruo na mmechi. Kọwaa ihe mere i ji tinye akụkụ dị n’etiti ebe ahụ.
questions.answer: B, C, A. C dị n’etiti n’ihi na ọ bụ ozi leta ahụ; ọ na-esochi ekele ma na-abịa tupu mmechi.
questions.explanation: Only the three supplied message sections are being ordered. This is not a claim that these three sections alone form a complete national letter-writing layout.

markingGuide.description: Places B first as the salutation.
Places C next as the message and A last as the closing.
Explains that the message follows the greeting and precedes the closing.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Copy a provided teacher model of a personal letter while preserving its wording and layout.
questions.prompt: Kọpịa leta onye nkụzi nyere gị. Debe okwu niile, akara edemede na nhazi akụkụ ya.
questions.answer:
Ụlọ Akwụkwọ Ọganihu,
Enugu.
19 Novemba 2026.

Ezigbo enyi m Adaeze,
Kedụ ka ị mere? Anyị nwere akwụkwọ ọhụrụ n’ụlọ akwụkwọ. Akwụkwọ ndị a na-akọ maka anụmanụ. Ọ na-atọ m ụtọ ịgụ ha.

Enyi gị,
Obinna.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Write an original personal letter with an appropriate familiar audience, purpose and organisation.
questions.prompt: Enyi gị nyeere gị aka ịghọta otu ihe n’akwụkwọ. Dee leta nkeonye n’asụsụ Igbo iji kelee ya. Kọwaa ihe o mere na otu o si nyere gị aka. Jiri aha na adreesị i chepụtara.
questions.answer:
Ụlọ Akwụkwọ Mmụta,
Nsukka.
19 Novemba 2026.

Ezigbo enyi m Oluchi,
Kedụ ka ị mere? Daalụ maka enyemaka gị. Ị kọwaara m okwu ndị dị n’akwụkwọ anyị. Ugbu a, aghọtara m ha. M ga-agụ akwụkwọ ahụ ọzọ.

Enyi gị,
Chinaza.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Write an original personal letter with an appropriate familiar audience, purpose and organisation.
questions.prompt: Ị chọrọ ịgụ akwụkwọ enyi gị nwere. Dee leta nkeonye rịọ ya ka o binye gị akwụkwọ ahụ. Kọwaa ihe mere i ji chọọ ya na otu ị ga-esi lekọta ya. Echepụtala na o kweelarị.
questions.answer:
Ụlọ Akwụkwọ Ọganihu,
Aba.
19 Novemba 2026.

Ezigbo enyi m Uche,
Biko, ị nwere ike ibinye m akwụkwọ gị gbasara osisi? Achọrọ m ịmụtakwu maka osisi. M ga-edebe akwụkwọ ahụ ọcha. Agaghị m ede ihe n’ime ya. M ga-eweghachi ya mgbe m gụchara ya. Daalụ.

Enyi gị,
Nneoma.
questions.explanation: A request asks for permission rather than presuming agreement; the writer gives a reason and proposes care of the borrowed item.

markingGuide.description: Uses an appropriate personal-letter opening and closing with fictional details.
Makes a clear, courteous request to borrow the book.
Provides a relevant reason for wanting it.
States at least one concrete care action.
Uses coherent intelligible Igbo without presenting permission as already given.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.learningObjective: Write an original personal letter with an appropriate familiar audience, purpose and organisation.
questions.prompt: Gụọ ozi enyi gị. Dee leta nzaghachi n’asụsụ Igbo. Gwa ya na ị gaghị abịa, kọwaa ihe kpatara ya, ma tụọ oge ọzọ unu ga-agụkọ akwụkwọ. Ị nwere ike ichepụta ihe kpatara ya.
questions.answer:
Ụlọ Akwụkwọ Mmụta,
Enugu.
19 Novemba 2026.

Ezigbo enyi m Chika,
Daalụ maka ịkpọ m òkù. Agaghị m abịa n’ehihie echi n’ihi na m ga-enyere nne m aka. Anyị nwere ike ịgụkọ akwụkwọ n’ụbọchị ọzọ. Ka anyị gụọ ya n’ụtụtụ Satọdee.

Enyi gị,
Kene.
questions.explanation: The reply responds to an invitation, declines clearly, gives a fictional reason and proposes a different reading time. This is language practice, not an actual meeting arrangement.

markingGuide.description: Addresses Chika in a suitable personal-letter opening and includes a closing/sender.
Acknowledges the invitation and clearly declines the proposed visit.
Gives a relevant reason in intelligible Igbo.
Proposes a different intelligible day/time for reading together.
Organises a coherent Igbo reply that fits the invitation.

questions.subject: Igbo Language
questions.topic: Mkpụrụokwu ndị metụtara mmekọrịta ndị mmadụ na ibe ha
questions.learningObjective: Use appropriate greetings and responses to maintain a short interpersonal conversation in Igbo.
questions.prompt: Gị na onye nkụzi ga-eme nkenke ejije. Ị hụrụ enyi gị n’ụtụtụ. Kelee ya, zaa ajụjụ ọ ga-ajụ banyere otú ị mere, jụọkwa otú o mere. Jiri asụsụ Igbo.
questions.answer: Ụtụtụ ọma. Onye nkụzi: Kedụ ka ị mere? Azịza: Ọ dị mma. Kedụ maka gị?
questions.explanation: A greeting exchange requires a context-appropriate greeting, a response and a reciprocal enquiry. Equivalent courteous Igbo forms are acceptable; no prescribed gesture or gender role is required.

markingGuide.description: Uses an intelligible greeting appropriate to meeting a friend in the morning.
Responds appropriately when the examiner asks how the learner is.
Asks a reciprocal enquiry and allows the partner to respond.

questions.languageReviewNote: Independent Igbo linguistic/academic review is pending. Underdots are meaningful; these contextual writing tasks do not prescribe a complete tone-marking system. Accept equivalent intelligible Igbo forms and regional variants after examiner checking. Local school orthographic conventions and marking calibration remain unverified.
questions.teacherSupport: Examiner plays the friend, responds to the greeting and asks “Kedụ ka ị mere?” before answering the learner’s reciprocal question. No handshake, bowing, kneeling or physical contact is scored. A fictional response is permitted.
questions.deliveryNote: Require a live examiner or individual recording. Examiner prepares and checks the Igbo wording, allows a fictional identity and scores the stated communicative features. Written preparation alone is insufficient. No actual performance, reference audio, tone testing, universal accent standard or examiner calibration is claimed.
